run_program.description: galago-compatible: upload script_content as a protocol, start a run of it and wait until it ends (upload_protocol, start_run, get_run_status). The deck must match the protocol.

variables.description: Not supported by LabMCP: leave empty

max_setpoint.description: Largest setpoint magnitude, in the controller's own setpoint units

close_valve.description:
Stop the flow: set the flow setpoint to 0 and hold all valves closed (Alicat HC). Safe to
call at any time. On pressure controllers the pressure setpoint is left unchanged and the
valves are held closed, trapping the current pressure.

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_device_info.description:
Report model, serial number, firmware, calibration date, whether the device is a
controller, the units of every data-frame field, the setpoint full scale and setpoint source.

hold_valve.description:
Freeze the controller's valve(s) at their current position (HLD): closed-loop control stops,
so flow will drift if upstream pressure changes. Use `resume_control` to release, or
`close_valve` to shut off completely.

list_gases.description:
List the gases installed on this mass flow device (number and short name), as used by
`set_gas`. Liquid and pressure-only devices have no gas list.

log_flow_series.description:
Record a time series of data frames (e.g. to check flow stability, settling after a
setpoint change, or pressure drift). Returns every point plus mean/stdev/min/max of the
mass flow (or the main measured quantity for non-flow devices).

save_path.description: Optional new .csv file for the full series (an existing file is not overwritten)

read_flow.description:
Read the live data frame: mass flow, volumetric flow, pressure, temperature, setpoint
(controllers), active gas and any status codes, each with the device's engineering units.

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

resume_control.description:
Cancel any valve hold and resume closed-loop control to the current setpoint. Flow restarts
immediately if the setpoint is not 0 (check it with `read_flow` first).

set_flow_setpoint.description:
Change the controller setpoint: starts, changes or stops gas flow (or sets the target
pressure on a pressure controller). 0 stops flow and closes the valve on a flow controller.
Negative values only work on bidirectional controllers. Refused on meters, above the
`max_setpoint` limit, and above the device's full scale.

setpoint.description: New setpoint in the controller's setpoint units (see get_device_info)

set_gas.description:
Select the gas calibration the mass flow device uses (Gas Select). This changes how flow is
computed, so do it with the setpoint at 0. Only gases installed on the device work (see
`list_gases`); corrosive gases need anti-corrosive (S-series) hardware.

gas.description: Gas short name or number, e.g. 'N2' (8), 'Air' (0), 'O2' (11), 'CO2' (4), 'Ar' (1), 'He' (7), 'H2' (6), 'CH4' (2); COMPOSER mixes are 236-255

save_as_power_up.description: Also make it the power-up gas (10v05+)

tare_flow.description:
Tare (zero) the flow reading. ONLY run with no flow through the device: upstream shut off
or controller setpoint 0, with the line at its normal operating pressure. Refused if the
setpoint is not 0 or a significant flow is still being measured.

tare_pressure.description:
Tare a pressure reading. Requires no flow and the device OPEN TO ATMOSPHERE (gauge), or no
flow and an unpressurised process line (absolute, barometer-equipped devices only).

kind.description: 'gauge' zeroes a gauge/differential sensor; 'absolute' aligns the absolute sensor to the built-in barometer (barometer option required)

clear_results.description:
Delete all received messages and results from this server's memory (e.g. between runs).

The optional JSONL store file is not modified. Nothing is sent to the analyzer.

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_connection_status.description:
Report the analyzer link state, the messages and results received, and link-layer error
counters.

Shows the link (serial / TCP client / TCP listener), whether an analyzer is connected, whether
a transmission is in progress, and NAKed frames, checksum errors and retransmissions.

get_result_detail.description:
Show every decoded field of one result, with its comments, order and patient context, raw
records and message header.

Includes universal test ID components, operator, start/completion times, instrument,
priority and specimen type. Patient identifiers stay redacted unless disabled at launch.

get_results.description:
Return received results, filtered by sample ID, patient ID, test code, time received or
abnormal flag (newest last).

Each result has its value exactly as transmitted, units, reference range, flags, status and
any comment records that followed it.

abnormal_only.description: Only results with an abnormal flag other than N

limit.description: Most recent matching results to return

patient_id.description: Patient ID as sent by the analyzer (exact match)

since.description: Only results received at/after this ISO 8601 time (UTC if no zone)

test_code.description: Analyzer test code, e.g. WBC, GLU, TSH (case-insensitive)

list_received_messages.description:
List the most recent ASTM messages received (newest last).

Each entry shows the analyzer, number of records and results, sample IDs, whether the
message was complete, and any parser warnings.

since.description: Only messages received at/after this ISO 8601 time (UTC if no zone)

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

calibrate.description:
Store one calibration point. The probe must already be in the named standard (buffer,
air, dry, ...) with a stable reading. Point names are validated per circuit type. pH: a `mid`
calibration erases existing low/high points, so always do mid first. EC: do `dry` first.

point.description: pH: mid|low|high; ORP: single; DO: atmospheric|zero; EC: dry|single|low|high; RTD: single; CO2: zero|high; PRS: zero|high

value.description: Value of the standard the probe is in (pH units, mV, µS/cm, temperature in the RTD's current scale, ppm CO2, pressure in current units). Omit for DO atmospheric/zero, EC dry and CO2/PRS zero.

clear_calibration.description:
Delete all stored calibration data (Cal,clear). pH/ORP/DO/EC/RTD return to uncalibrated;
CO2/PRS return to their factory calibration. The probe must be recalibrated afterwards.

get_calibration_status.description:
Report how many calibration points are stored and what that means for this circuit type;
for pH also the probe slope (acid/base % of ideal and zero offset in mV).

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_info.description:
Report the circuit type, firmware, device name, supply voltage and last restart reason,
LED state, calibration state, temperature compensation and type-specific settings (enabled
outputs, EC probe constant K, DO salinity/pressure compensation).

log_series.description:
Record a series of readings (e.g. to watch a probe stabilise before calibrating, follow pH
or DO in a bioreactor, or log temperature). Returns every point plus mean, stdev, min, max
and drift per minute for each output.

save_path.description: Optional new .csv file for the full series (never overwritten)

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_do_compensation.description:
DO circuits only: set salinity compensation (irrelevant below ~2500 µS/cm) and/or
atmospheric pressure compensation (default 101.3 kPa; lower at altitude). Neither is
retained through a power cycle.

set_led.description: Turn the circuit's status LED on or off. Returns the new LED state.

on.description: True = LED on (default), False = off (e.g. light-sensitive cultures)

set_probe_constant.description:
EC circuits only: set the conductivity probe's cell constant K to match the probe
(printed on it). Recalibrate after changing it. Returns the K now in use.

k.description: Cell constant K of the EC probe (e.g. 0.1, 1.0, 10)

set_temperature_compensation.description:
Set the sample temperature used to compensate pH, EC or DO readings (T,n; always °C).
Not retained through a power cycle. Returns the value the circuit now uses.

max_current_a.description: Largest current-limit setpoint on any channel

max_voltage_v.description: Largest voltage setpoint (magnitude) on any channel

labmcp-bench-psu.server: Bench DC Power Supply (Rigol / Siglent / Aim-TTi)

all_outputs_off.description:
Switch every output OFF (emergency stop for the whole supply). Each channel is switched
individually and read back where the instrument supports it.

clear_protection_trip.description:
Clear an OVP/OCP trip after fixing its cause. The output stays OFF; use `output_on` to
re-energise. On Aim-TTi supplies this clears trips on all outputs.

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_errors.description: Read (and clear) the instrument's error queue / error registers. Empty list = no errors.

get_outputs.description:
Report each channel: voltage and current-limit setpoints, measured voltage/current/power,
output on/off, CV/CC mode, and OVP/OCP levels and trip state where the model supports them.

channel.description: One channel, or omit for all

output_off.description: Switch a channel's output OFF. Safe to call at any time.

output_on.description:
Switch a channel's output ON, energising the connected load at the present setpoints.
The setpoints are read back first and the output is refused if they exceed the safety limits
(e.g. after someone changed them on the front panel).

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_current_limit.description:
Set a channel's current limit (the constant-current setpoint). Refused above `max_current_a`
(checked even with the output off) or above the channel's range.

set_protection.description:
Set over-voltage (OVP) and/or over-current (OCP) protection for a channel. When exceeded,
the supply switches the output off. Rigol: levels + on/off; Aim-TTi CPX/QL/PL-P: levels (always
armed), MX: levels + on/off; Siglent SPD1000X: levels only; SPD3303X: not available.

enabled.description: Switch OVP/OCP on or off (models that allow it)

set_voltage.description:
Set a channel's voltage setpoint. Refused above `max_voltage_v` (checked even with the output
off) or above the channel's range. If the output is on, the load sees the new voltage at once.

voltage_v.description: Voltage setpoint in V (negative only on negative channels)

max_wait_s.description: Longest wait for a measurement (BP, temperature, weight, spot-check)

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_device_info.description:
Read the device's identity (manufacturer, model, serial, firmware), the standard health
services it exposes and its features.

Features include the body sensor location, supported oximeter / blood-pressure status flags,
scale resolution and thermometer site.

read_battery.description: Read the device's battery level (Battery Service, 0-100 %).

read_pulse_oximetry.description:
Read SpO2 (%) and pulse rate from a pulse oximeter, averaged over a few seconds or as a
single spot-check reading.

Continuous mode listens for `duration_s` and returns the latest valid values plus mean/min;
spot-check mode waits for the oximeter's single stable reading. Early packets are often NaN
while the sensor acquires; these are counted in `unavailable_samples`, never reported as values.

duration_s.description: Continuous mode: seconds to average over

mode.description: auto: connect, then continuous if the oximeter supports it, else wait for a spot-check. spot_check: wait for a reading even if the oximeter is not advertising yet

timeout_s.description: Spot-check mode: seconds to wait

read_temperature.description:
Wait for a thermometer to send a temperature measurement and return it in °C.

°F readings are converted; the measurement site is included if the device reports one.

accept_intermediate.description: If no final measurement arrives before the timeout, return the latest Intermediate Temperature value (probe still settling) instead of an error

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for a measurement

read_weight.description:
Wait for a scale to send a weight measurement (kg), with BMI and height if the scale sends
them.

Ask the person to step on the scale after calling this. lb readings are converted to kg.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for a measurement

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

record_heart_rate.description:
Record heart rate for `duration_s`: bpm series, RR intervals and time-domain HRV (mean HR,
SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50).

The sensor must be worn with good skin contact. HRV statistics are for research, not clinical
ECG analysis. Use `save_path` to keep every packet as CSV.

max_points.description: Max points returned per series

save_path.description: Optional new .csv file for the full recording (never overwrites a file)

scan_devices.description:
Scan for nearby Bluetooth LE devices: address, name, signal strength and advertised health
services. Works without a configured --address.

Devices only show up while advertising (monitors often advertise only right after a
measurement), and some do not list every service in their advertisement, so `service`
filtering can miss them.

service.description: Only list devices advertising this service

timeout_s.description: How long to listen for advertisements

wait_for_blood_pressure.description:
Wait for a blood pressure monitor to send a measurement: systolic, diastolic and mean
arterial pressure (mmHg) and pulse rate.

Call this, then ask the participant to start a measurement on the monitor. kPa readings are
converted to mmHg; the unit sent is reported. Older stored readings are listed separately.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for a measurement

max_record_duration_s.description: Longest recording/analysis window an agent may request

configure_board.description:
Send a raw board-specific command to the firmware through BrainFlow's config_board (e.g.
OpenBCI channel settings 'x1060110X', test signals, or Muse presets 'p50'/'p61' to enable PPG).

The string is passed through unchecked: besides acquisition settings, some commands switch on
outputs such as the lead-off (impedance-test) current that flows through the participant's
electrodes. Settings persist until another command changes them or the board is power-cycled
(stopping the stream does not undo them). Consult the board's SDK documentation first and tell
the user what the command does.

get_band_powers.description:
EEG band powers (delta 1-4, theta 4-8, alpha 8-13, beta 13-30, gamma 30-50 Hz) over the most
recent `window_s` seconds: BrainFlow's channel-averaged relative powers plus per-channel absolute
(uV^2) and relative powers and the peak frequency. Records a fresh window if not streaming.

window_s.description: Seconds of data to analyse (4 s recommended)

get_board_info.description:
Describe the connected board: channel names by type (EEG/EMG/ECG/EOG share the EXG rows on
most boards), sampling rate, available presets (data buffers) and streaming state.

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_signal_quality.description:
Check every EXG channel for common electrode problems: flat line (disconnected), railed
(amplifier saturated, OpenBCI Cyton boards), strong 50/60 Hz mains noise (poor contact or
missing reference), and implausibly high amplitude (movement, muscle, loose electrode).

insert_marker.description:
Write an event marker into the data stream at the current sample (for event-related
experiments: stimulus onsets, condition changes). Requires `start_streaming`; markers appear in
`record` results and saved files.

value.description: Event code written to the marker channel; must not be 0

list_supported_boards.description:
List common BrainFlow boards: the `--option board=` alias, BrainFlow board id, and which
connection detail `--address` must hold (serial port, Bluetooth MAC, IP address or serial number).
Any other BrainFlow BoardIds name or numeric id is accepted too. Does not need a board.

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

record.description:
Record `duration_s` seconds and return per-channel statistics, event markers and downsampled
traces. Uses the live stream if one is running, otherwise starts a temporary one. The full data
(every row, full sampling rate) can be written to `save_path`. `stop_streaming` ends a recording
early.

max_points.description: Max points per downsampled trace

remove_dc.description: Subtract each channel's mean from the traces

save_format.description: csv: labelled columns; brainflow: DataFilter.write_file format (replayable)

save_path.description: Write the full-resolution data (all rows) to this new file (.csv; never overwrites a file)

buffer_duration_s.description: Size of BrainFlow's ring buffer, in seconds of data

stop_streaming.description:
Stop acquisition (saves battery). A `record` in progress ends at once with the data acquired
so far. Data already in the buffer is kept until the next stream starts or the session is
released (`reconnect`).

max_flow_ul_s.description: Highest plunger flow rate an agent may use

max_volume_ul.description: Largest volume a single aspirate/dispense may move

aspirate_ul.description:
Draw `volume_ul` into the syringe at `flow_ul_s` through the current (or given) valve port,
and wait until the move has finished. The pump must be initialized and have room for the volume.

port.description: Distribution valves: port to turn to first

volume_ul.description: Volume to draw into the syringe, µL

dispense_ul.description:
Push `volume_ul` out of the syringe at `flow_ul_s` through the current (or given) valve port,
and wait until the move has finished. The syringe must contain at least that volume.

port.description: Distribution valves: port to turn to first

volume_ul.description: Volume to push out of the syringe, µL

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_status.description:
Report whether the pump is ready or busy, any error (decoded), the plunger position as the
volume in the syringe, the valve position, resolution mode and current top speed.

initialize.description:
Initialize the pump: drive the plunger to the top of the syringe (expelling its contents
through the valve), set that as position 0 and home the valve. Needed after power-up, a plunger
overload or `terminate`. Route the valve output to waste first. Takes a few seconds.

force.description: Plunger force against the syringe top; auto picks it from the syringe size

valve_direction.description: Valve homing/port numbering: cw (Z command), ccw (Y), or no_valve (W, plunger only)

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_valve.description:
Turn the valve to a named position (3/4-port valves) or to a numbered port (distribution
valves). In bypass the plunger cannot move. Returns the new status.

direction.description: Distribution valves: rotation direction to the port

position.description: Non-distribution valves: input, output, bypass or extra

terminate.description:
Stop any plunger move, loop or delay immediately (DT command T). A valve move in progress
still completes. Re-initialize afterwards: the plunger may have lost steps.

max_put_batch.description: Most PVs one put_pvs call may write

max_put_wait_s.description: Longest wait for a put-callback (completion) per write

apply_safe_state.description:
Emergency action: write the scientist-configured safe-state PVs (--option safe_state, e.g.
motor STOP fields, shutter close, HV off), all of them even if one fails. Available in read-only
mode. It does not replace the facility's own interlocks and stop buttons.

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_pv.description:
Read one PV with its metadata: value, units, precision, alarm severity/status, IOC timestamp
and age, display/alarm/warning/control limits and enum state names. Waveforms come back
downsampled with min/max/mean statistics.

max_elements.description: Arrays longer than this are downsampled

get_pvs.description:
Read many PVs at once (e.g. all motors or vacuum gauges of a beamline). PVs that cannot be
reached are listed in `errors` instead of failing the whole call.

max_elements.description: Arrays longer than this are downsampled

monitor_pv.description:
Subscribe to a PV and collect every value change for `duration_s` seconds (or until
`max_updates`), then return statistics (min/max/mean/std, drift rate) and the updates.

max_points.description: Updates to include in the reply (evenly thinned)

put_pv.description:
Write a PV. This can move motors, open shutters, change magnet or high-voltage setpoints and
heat or cool samples: tell the user exactly what will change first. The write is refused unless
the PV matches the put allow-list, the IOC grants write access, and the value has the right
type and lies within the PV's control limits (DRVL/DRVH). Returns the read-back value.

timeout_s.description: Max seconds to wait for completion

value.description: New value: number, enum state name or index, string, or array for waveforms

put_pvs.description:
Write several PVs in order (e.g. set both slit blades). Every write is validated first (allow-
list, access rights, type, control limits); if any is invalid nothing is written. Writing stops
at the first failure and the rest are reported as not written. The whole batch must finish within
an hour: writes that would start later are not sent.

timeout_s.description: Max seconds to wait per write

wait.description: Wait for each put-completion before the next write

value.description: Value (number, enum state, string or array)

pv_info.description:
Connection details of a PV: serving IOC host:port, native type, element count, and whether this
client has read/write access (EPICS access security) and passes the put allow-list.

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

max_speed_rpm.description: Highest stirring speed an agent may set

max_temperature_c.description: Highest hotplate temperature setpoint an agent may set

max_wait_s.description: Longest wait_for_temperature an agent may start

disable_watchdog.description:
Cancel watchdog mode 2 (OUT_WD2@0) and stop the background refresh. Watchdog mode 1 has
no cancel command; this tool reports an error for it.

enable_watchdog.description:
Arm the hotplate's communication watchdog (OUT_WD1@m / OUT_WD2@m). The server then
re-sends the watchdog command in the background; if the computer, this server or the cable
fails, the hotplate switches heating and stirring off (mode 1) or falls back to the given
safety values (mode 2) after `timeout_s`. Note: stopping or reconnecting the server also
stops the refresh, so the watchdog trips unless you enable it again. Mode 1 cannot be
cancelled over the interface.

mode.description: 1 = heater and motor off on timeout; 2 = fall back to the safety values below

safety_speed_rpm.description: Mode 2 only: speed to fall back to (OUT_SP_42@)

safety_temperature_c.description: Mode 2 only: setpoint to fall back to (OUT_SP_12@)

timeout_s.description: Watchdog time (IKA allows 20-1500 s)

Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_status.description:
Read temperatures, stirring speed and setpoints. On hotplates: plate and external-probe
temperature, temperature setpoint and the device's safety-circuit temperature. On overhead
stirrers: PT1000 probe temperature, torque and the speed/torque limits set on the device.

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_speed.description:
Set the stirring speed setpoint (OUT_SP_4). Does not start the motor; if it is already
running, the speed changes immediately. Refused above `max_speed_rpm` (and, on overhead
stirrers, above the speed limit set on the device).

set_temperature.description:
Set the hotplate temperature setpoint (OUT_SP_1). With an external probe connected this is
the target temperature of the medium. Does not start heating; if heating is already on, the
plate starts moving to the new setpoint immediately. Refused above `max_temperature_c` or
above the device's own safety-circuit temperature.

start_heating.description:
Switch the hotplate heater on (START_1). It heats towards the current setpoint, which is
checked against `max_temperature_c` first. Make sure the vessel and its contents can take
the setpoint temperature and that nothing flammable is near the plate.

start_stirring.description:
Start the stirring motor (START_4) at the current speed setpoint, which is checked against
`max_speed_rpm` first. Make sure the stir bar or impeller is in place and the vessel is
secured (a decoupled stir bar or an unclamped vessel can splash).

stop_all.description:
Emergency stop: switch the heater off (hotplates) and stop the motor. Every stop command
is sent even if one of them fails. Also ends a running `wait_for_temperature`.

stop_heating.description:
Switch the hotplate heater off (STOP_1). Stirring continues. The plate stays hot for a
long time after switching off.

stop_stirring.description: Stop the stirring motor (STOP_4). Heating (if on) continues.

wait_for_temperature.description:
Poll a temperature until it is within `tolerance_c` of the target for `stable_for_s`
seconds, or until `timeout_s` passes. Does not change anything on the device (start heating
first). Returns whether the target was reached plus a short temperature trace. A stop
command ends the wait early.

sensor.description: 'external' = probe in the medium (IN_PV_1, or IN_PV_3 on overhead stirrers)

stable_for_s.description: Must stay within tolerance this long

target_c.description: Temperature to wait for; default: the current setpoint

timeout_s.description: Give up after this many seconds

max_temperature_c.description: Highest setpoint an agent may set

max_wait_s.description: Longest wait_for_temperature an agent may start

min_temperature_c.description: Lowest setpoint an agent may set

Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:

whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_setpoint.description: Read the current temperature setpoint and whether temperature control is running.

get_status.description:
Report the circulator's status message (decoded: operating state, rejected command or
alarm), whether temperature control is running, the setpoint, the device's own
excess-temperature protection setting and warning limits, and the firmware version.

read_temperatures.description:
Read the bath temperature, the heating/cooling power in % and the safety-sensor
temperature, and optionally the external Pt100 sensor.

include_external.description: Also read the external Pt100 sensor (MAGIO/DYNEO; not CORIO)

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_setpoint.description:
Set the circulator's temperature setpoint (out_sp_00). If temperature control is running,
the circulator starts heating or cooling to it immediately. Refused outside
`min_temperature_c`..`max_temperature_c`; the circulator itself also rejects values outside
its range or warning limits (reported as an error). Needs remote control enabled.

start_circulation.description:
Start temperature control (out_mode_05 1): the pump runs and the bath heats or cools to
the setpoint, which is checked against the safety limits first (it may have been changed on
the front panel). Make sure the bath is filled and any external hoses are connected and
secured. Needs remote control enabled.

stop_circulation.description:
Stop temperature control and the pump (out_mode_05 0), then confirm with in_mode_05.
Also ends a running `wait_for_temperature`. The bath stays hot/cold after stopping.

wait_for_temperature.description:
Poll the bath (or external) temperature until it has been within `tolerance_c` of the
target for `stable_for_s` seconds, or `timeout_s` passes. Does not change anything; start
circulation first. Stops early (reached = false) if the circulator raises an alarm or a
stop command is sent. Returns a short temperature trace.

stable_for_s.description: Must stay within tolerance this long

target_c.description: Temperature to wait for; default: the current setpoint

timeout_s.description: Give up after this many seconds

max_current_a.description: Largest |current| an agent may source or allow as compliance

max_power_w.description: Largest worst-case power |source level x compliance|

max_sweep_points.description: Most points (including the return leg) in one IV sweep

max_voltage_v.description: Largest |voltage| an agent may source or allow as compliance

configure_source.description:
Set up the source (function, level, compliance, range, measurement speed) while the output
is OFF. Measures V and I with auto-ranging. Refused if the output is on; turn it off first or
use `set_source_level`. Limits are checked before anything is sent.

compliance.description: Limit: current limit in A (voltage source) or voltage limit in V (current source)

level.description: Source level: volts for a voltage source, amps for a current source

nplc.description: Measurement integration time in power-line cycles (1 = 16.7/20 ms)

source_range.description: Fixed source range (V or A); omit for auto-range

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_device_info.description:
Identify the SMU: manufacturer, model, serial, firmware, command dialect (2400 / 2450 /
2600), channel (2600B) and the model's maximum source voltage and current.

get_status.description:
Report whether the output is on, the source function (voltage/current), programmed level,
compliance limit, whether the source is in compliance, terminals and 2/4-wire sense.

measure.description:
Take one source-measure reading (voltage, current, V/I, power, compliance flag) of the
energised DUT. Does not change any setting; refused if the output is off.

output_off.description:
Switch the SMU output OFF immediately (and abort any IV sweep in progress). Always
available, including in read-only mode.

output_on.description:
Switch the SMU output ON: the configured voltage or current is applied to the DUT. The
programmed level and compliance are read back from the instrument and checked against the
safety limits first. Confirm with the user that the DUT is connected and safe to energise.

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

run_iv_sweep.description:
Run a stepped IV sweep: configure the source, switch the output ON, step through the
levels measuring V and I at each, then ALWAYS switch the output OFF (also on errors or when
`output_off` is called). Returns the curve (downsampled), compliance flags, a linear fit and
optional full CSV (a new file; an existing file is never overwritten). The output must be off
beforehand. Limits are checked first.

compliance.description: Current limit in A (voltage sweep) or voltage limit in V (current sweep)

delay_s.description: Settling delay at each point, s

dual.description: Sweep back from stop to start afterwards (hysteresis)

max_points.description: Maximum points returned in the reply

save_path.description: Optional CSV path for every point

start.description: First level: V (voltage sweep) or A (current sweep)

stop_on_compliance.description: End the sweep at the first compliance point

set_4wire.description:
Select 4-wire (remote sense, Kelvin) or 2-wire measurement. 4-wire removes lead
resistance for low-resistance DUTs but needs the SENSE leads connected. Refused while the
output is on.

enabled.description: True = 4-wire remote sense, False = 2-wire local sense

set_source_level.description:
Change the level of the configured source. If the output is ON the new voltage/current is
applied to the DUT immediately. The level and the present compliance are checked against the
safety limits first.

level.description: New level for the configured source: V or A

max_dac_voltage_v.description: Highest DAC output voltage an agent may set

max_scan_rate_hz.description: Highest stream scan rate (scans/s, all channels per scan)

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_device_info.description:
Identify the connected LabJack (model, serial, firmware, connection) and list what it
offers: analog inputs, valid input ranges, resolution indices, DAC range, digital lines and
stream rate. Call this before configuring channels.

read_analog_inputs.description:
Read one or more analog inputs once (command-response) and return volts.

Range and resolution settings persist on the device until changed. On the T8, several
channels are sampled simultaneously. Each reading reports what it was measured against
(GND or the negative input). Fails while a stream is running.

differential.description: T7 only: true = measure AINn - AIN(n+1) for even n (e.g. AIN0-AIN1), false = single-ended, omit = keep the current setting

range_v.description: ± input range in V for all listed channels (T7: 10/1/0.1/0.01; T8: 11 ... 0.018). Omit to keep the current range. Not settable on the T4.

resolution_index.description: Higher = less noise, slower (T4 0-5, T7 0-8, T7-Pro 0-12, T8 0-16; 0 = default). Omit to keep.

read_device_temperature.description:
Read the LabJack's internal temperature sensor (°C, about ±2 °C) and the estimated ambient
air temperature. On the T8 also returns the sensor next to each AIN terminal. Cannot be read
while a stream is running.

read_digital_inputs.description:
Report the logic level and direction (input/output/analog) of digital I/O lines.

Uses the DIO_STATE/DIO_DIRECTION bitmask registers, which never change a line's direction, so
it is safe to call while lines are driving equipment. Outputs report the level actually on the
terminal.

lines.description: Lines to report, e.g. ['FIO0', 'EIO3'] or ['DIO4']. Omit for all lines.

read_thermocouple.description:
Read a thermocouple with the T7/T8 AIN thermocouple extended feature (types B, C, E, J, K,
N, R, S, T) and return °C with the measured voltage and cold-junction temperature.

This configures the AIN extended feature on the channel (the T7 switches a ±10 V range to
±0.1 V). A floating/open thermocouple returns valid=false. Accuracy is dominated by the CJC:
about ±2 °C with the internal sensor. Not available on the T4.

channel.description: AIN the thermocouple + lead is on

cjc.description: Cold-junction sensor: 'internal' (device sensor; best for T7 screw terminals / T8) or 'lm34' (LM34 on cjc_channel, e.g. on a CB37)

cjc_channel.description: AIN of the LM34 when cjc='lm34'

differential.description: T7 only: thermocouple between AINn (+) and AIN(n+1) (-); recommended on the CB37

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_digital_output.description:
Make a digital line an output and drive it high (3.3 V) or low (0 V).

Digital outputs often switch relays, solid-state relays, valves or instrument trigger inputs,
so confirm with the user what the line controls. The line keeps driving until changed or
released with `set_outputs_safe`.

set_outputs_safe.description:
Put the outputs in a safe state: stop any stream, set DAC0 and DAC1 to 0 V, and release
every digital line this server drove (plus the `safe_dio` option lines) to input - or drive
them low with dio_mode='low'. Use when finished or if anything looks wrong.

dio_mode.description: 'input' (default) returns lines to the power-up state (input with pull-up); 'low' drives them to 0 V instead

stream_analog.description:
Acquire a hardware-timed waveform on one or more analog inputs (LJM stream mode) and return
per-channel statistics plus a downsampled waveform; optionally save everything to CSV.

Bounded by the `max_stream_duration_s` and `max_scan_rate_hz` limits and the device maximum
(T4 50 kS/s, T7 100 kS/s aggregate, T8 40 kscans/s). On the T8, list adjacent channels in
order; on the T7 the streamed inputs are set to single-ended. Blocks for `duration_s`;
`set_outputs_safe` stops a running stream early.

max_points.description: Max points per channel in the returned waveform

range_v.description: ± range in V for all channels (T7/T8); omit to keep

resolution_index.description: Stream resolution index; omit for default

save_path.description: Write the full-resolution data to this new .csv file (never overwritten)

scan_rate_hz.description: Scans per second (one sample of every channel per scan). At least 1, so set_outputs_safe can stop the stream within a second; use read_analog_inputs for slower logging

write_dac.description:
Set an analog output (DAC0/DAC1) to a DC voltage. The output stays at this value until
changed or `set_outputs_safe` is called.

This energises whatever is wired to the DAC (a heater driver, valve, laser or motor
controller input). Checked against `max_dac_voltage_v` and the model's hardware range before
anything is sent. The DAC can source about 20 mA through 50 Ohm; loads pull the voltage down.

max_setpoint_k.description: Highest control setpoint an agent may set

all_heaters_off.description:
Turn every output off (heater range 0 on outputs 1-4), like the front-panel All Off key,
and stop any running wait. Reports the read-back range of each output and `all_off`.

get_command_log.description:
Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_heater_status.description:
Report each output's control mode and input, heater range, output %, setpoint (and in
kelvin), ramp state, PID values and heater errors (open/short). Reading a heater error clears
it on the controller.

read_temperatures.description:
Read every (or the selected) sensor input: kelvin, raw sensor units, sensor type, input
name and decoded reading status (invalid, under/overrange). Disabled inputs are listed with
null readings.

inputs.description: Inputs to read (default: all inputs of the model)

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_heater_range.description:
Set an output's heater range (each step is ~10x more power). Anything above 0 lets the
output heat: in closed loop as the PID demands, in open loop at the front-panel manual output.
Refused above `max_heater_range`, or if the setpoint already programmed on a closed-loop, zone
or warm-up output is above `max_setpoint_k`. Start with the lowest range that can reach the
setpoint.

heater_range.description: 0 = off; 335/336: 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high; 350: 1-5; outputs 3/4: 1 = on

set_pid.description: Set the P, I and D values of an output's control loop (Lake Shore conventions).

set_ramp.description:
Turn setpoint ramping on or off for an output's control loop and set the rate. With ramping
on, the next setpoint change moves the setpoint gradually - gentler on samples and wiring.

enabled.description: Ramp the setpoint instead of stepping it

set_setpoint.description:
Set the control setpoint of an output's loop in kelvin. If setpoint ramping is on, the
setpoint moves toward the new value at the ramp rate. Heating only happens if the output is in
closed-loop mode and its heater range is not off. Refused above `max_setpoint_k`.

wait_for_stable_temperature.description:
Wait until the control input of `output` has stayed within `tolerance_k` of the setpoint
(and the setpoint is no longer ramping) for `stable_for_s`, or until `timeout_s`. Returns
whether it stabilised, the final temperature and a downsampled trace. Changes nothing.

output.description: Control loop whose setpoint and input are used

stable_for_s.description: How long T must stay within tolerance

timeout_s.description: Give up after this long

Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:
Report which instrument is connected (identity, address, simulated or real),
whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_draft_shield.description: Report the position of the motorised draft-shield doors (Excellence/XPR balances only).

get_tare.description: Return the weight currently stored in the tare memory.

log_weight_series.description:
Record a series of immediate (unfiltered) readings to monitor drift, evaporation,
moisture uptake or stabilisation. Returns every reading plus summary statistics.

read_temperature.description: Read the balance's internal temperature probe(s) in °C (MT-SICS M28, if supported).

read_weight.description: Read the current net weight from the balance.

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

reset_balance.description:
Abort whatever the balance is doing (an adjustment, a repeating weight stream, a pending
command) and reset it to its power-on state without zeroing (MT-SICS @). Clears the tare.
Motorised draft-shield doors have their own obstruction detection and reverse if blocked.

run_internal_adjustment.description:
Adjust (calibrate) the balance with its built-in reference weight (MT-SICS C3).
The pan must be empty and the balance undisturbed. Takes roughly 1-3 minutes.

set_draft_shield.description:
Open or close the motorised draft-shield doors. Make sure nothing (and no one's
fingers) is in the way of the doors.

set_tare_preset.description: Preset a known tare weight (e.g. a container weighed earlier).

unit.description: Must be the balance's unit 1, usually 'g'

show_message.description:
Show a short message on the balance display (e.g. 'Add sample 3'). Use
`show_weight_display` to return to the normal weight display.

text.description: Text for the balance display; '' clears it

show_weight_display.description: Switch the balance display back to showing the weight.

tare.description:
Tare the balance: store the current load (e.g. an empty container) as the tare weight.
Returns the stored tare weight.

immediately.description: Tare now even if unstable (less accurate). Default waits for stability.

zero.description: Zero the balance with the current load. Also clears the tare memory.

immediately.description: Zero now even if the reading is unstable

max_frames.description: Most images in one z-stack or time-lapse

max_xy_step_um.description: Largest XY stage move (distance) in one step

max_z_step_um.description: Largest focus (Z) move away from the current position

acquire_time_lapse.description:
Acquire a time-lapse at the current position: images every `interval_s` (optionally several
channels per timepoint), saves a multi-page TIFF and reports per-frame statistics and the intensity
change (bleaching). Bounded by `max_frames` and `max_acquisition_duration_s`; `stop_stage` aborts it.

channel_group.description: Config group of the channels; default: channel group

channels.description: Channel presets to image at every timepoint; omit for current settings

include_preview.description: Return a preview of the last frame

save_path.description: Multi-page TIFF path (ImageJ hyperstack, TCYX)

acquire_z_stack.description:
Acquire a z-stack around the current focus: moves Z through the slices (optionally imaging
several channels at each), saves a multi-page TIFF, reports per-slice statistics and the sharpest
slice, and returns Z to where it started. Every slice must stay within `max_z_step_um` of the start
and the Z soft limits.

channel_group.description: Config group of the channels; default: channel group

channels.description: Channel presets to image at every slice; omit for current settings

end_offset_um.description: Last slice relative to the current Z (e.g. +10)

save_path.description: Multi-page TIFF path (ImageJ hyperstack, ZCYX)

start_offset_um.description: First slice relative to the current Z (e.g. -10)

autofocus.description:
Run the configured autofocus device (e.g. a hardware focus lock) once; it moves the focus drive.
If the result is outside the Z step or soft limits, the focus is moved back and an error is raised.

close_shutter.description: Close the shutter (stop illuminating the sample) and abort any running acquisition.

whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_exposure.description: Return the camera exposure time in milliseconds.

get_position.description:
Read the XY stage and focus (Z) positions in micrometres, and which way increasing Z moves
the objective.

get_system_info.description:
Describe the microscope: loaded devices (camera, stages, shutters, filter wheels...), which
device has which role, camera size/bit depth/exposure, pixel size, config groups with their
presets, the current position, and the soft limits. Call this first.

list_config_groups.description:
List Micro-Manager config groups (e.g. Channel, Objective) with their presets and the preset
currently active.

move_stage_xy.description:
Move the XY stage. Moves longer than `max_xy_step_um` or outside the XY soft limits are refused
before anything moves. Make sure the objective and condenser clear the sample holder.

relative.description: Interpret x_um/y_um as offsets from the current position

x_um.description: Target X (µm), or the X offset if relative=True

y_um.description: Target Y (µm), or the Y offset if relative=True

move_z.description:
Move the focus drive (Z). Moving the objective toward the sample can crash it into the slide:
moves larger than `max_z_step_um` or outside the Z soft limits are refused before anything moves.

relative.description: Interpret z_um as an offset from the current position

z_um.description: Target focus position (µm), or the offset if relative=True

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_config.description:
Apply a config-group preset (e.g. switch the channel: filter cube, light source, emission
filter). Objective/turret groups are refused here: use `set_objective`.

set_exposure.description:
Set the camera exposure time (ms). Longer exposures give brighter images but more
photobleaching. Returns the exposure the camera accepted.

set_objective.description:
Switch the objective (rotates the nosepiece/turret). A longer or immersion objective can hit the
sample holder or need oil/water: confirm with the user first. Pixel size changes with the objective.

set_shutter.description:
Open or close the current shutter, and optionally switch auto-shutter. An open shutter
illuminates (and bleaches) the sample until it is closed again.

auto_shutter.description: Also set auto-shutter (open only during exposures). Leave on normally.

open.description: True opens the shutter (sample illuminated continuously)

snap_image.description:
Acquire one image with the current channel, exposure and position. The sample is illuminated
during the exposure. Saves the full image as TIFF and returns summary statistics (min/max/mean,
saturation, sharpness) plus an optional contrast-stretched preview.

include_preview.description: Return a small PNG preview image

save_path.description: TIFF path for the full image; default: a timestamped file in data_dir

stop_stage.description: Immediately stop XY and Z stage motion and abort any z-stack or time-lapse in progress.

apply_safe_state.description:
Put the device into the safe state defined in the register map (e.g. heater output
off, controller to standby), writing each step in order and reading it back. Every
step is attempted even if an earlier one fails. Call it immediately if anything looks
wrong. `all_ok` is true only if every step was written AND read back with the requested
value; a step the device acknowledged but ignored (e.g. in local mode) is not ok.

Return the most recent raw commands sent to / replies received from the
instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

get_connection_info.description:

whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

list_points.description:
Describe the loaded register map: device, every named point (table, 0-based address,
type, scaling, unit, writable, min/max, enum) and the safe-state steps. Works without a
connection.

read_coils.description: Read coils (FC01): single-bit outputs such as run/stop or relay states.

read_discrete_inputs.description: Read discrete inputs (FC02): single-bit, read-only status such as alarms or limit switches.

read_points.description:
Read named points from the register map, decoded and scaled into engineering units
(e.g. process_temperature = 25.1 °C). A point that cannot be read gets an `error`
instead of failing the whole call.

names.description: Point names from list_points; omit for all points

read_registers.description:
Read raw holding or input registers (unsigned 16-bit), optionally decoded as int16,
32-bit or 64-bit values. For exploring a device; prefer read_points when a register map
describes it.

decode_as.description: Also decode the registers as this type

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

write_coil.description:
Switch one raw coil (FC05). Coils often start or stop equipment (heaters, pumps,
motors); mapped coils are refused here (use write_point).

write_point.description:
Write a named point from the register map (setpoint, mode, output enable...). The value
is checked against the point's writable flag, min/max or enum BEFORE sending, converted
to raw registers, written, then read back. Changing setpoints and outputs acts on real
equipment. If the write succeeds but the read-back fails, `read_back_error` says why.

value.description: Engineering value (e.g. 37.5 for °C), true/false, or an enum label

write_register.description:
Write one raw holding register (FC06). No scaling or limits are applied, so only use it
for addresses the register map does not describe (mapped addresses are refused: use
write_point). Returns a read-back if the register is readable.

write_registers.description:
Write consecutive raw holding registers (FC16), e.g. both halves of a 32-bit value.
No scaling or limits are applied; mapped addresses are refused (use write_point).

max_conversion_time_s.description: Longest time a vendor-file conversion may run

max_xic_targets.description: Most m/z values in one extract_ion_chromatogram call

labmcp-ms-data.server: Mass Spectrometry Data (mzML, Bruker TDF, vendor conversion)

convert_to_mzml.description:
Convert a vendor file (Thermo .raw, Waters .raw, Agilent .d, SCIEX .wiff, Shimadzu .lcd,
Bruker .d) to mzML with the converter the user installed (ThermoRawFileParser, ProteoWizard
msconvert, or msconvert in Docker; chosen with --option converter=...). Writes a new file in
the data folder. Can take minutes; fails with install instructions if no converter is set up.

dry_run.description: Only show the command that would be run

output_folder.description: Folder for the .mzML, inside the data folder (default: next to the input)

path.description: Vendor file or folder (from list_runs), relative to the data folder

peak_picking.description: Centroid with the vendor algorithm during conversion

timeout_s.description: Give up after this many seconds

extract_ion_chromatogram.description:
Extracted ion chromatogram (XIC/EIC) for one or more m/z values: the summed intensity
within ± tolerance (ppm or Da) in every MS1 spectrum (or another `ms_level`). For each target
returns the apex RT and intensity, the apex peak's boundaries, area (intensity x min, no
baseline subtraction) and FWHM, plus a downsampled trace. Reads every spectrum in the RT
window, so restrict `rt_start_min`/`rt_end_min` on long runs.

max_points.description: Maximum points returned (downsampled, max per bin)

ms_level.description: MS level to use (1 = survey scans)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing save_path file

path.description: Run path relative to the data folder (from list_runs); may be omitted if there is one run

rt_end_min.description: Only use spectra at or before this RT (min)

rt_start_min.description: Only use spectra at or after this RT (min)

save_path.description: Optional new .csv file inside the data folder for the full-resolution data

find_ms2_scans.description:
Find the MS2 (MSn) spectra whose precursor m/z is within ± tolerance of `precursor_mz`,
optionally within an RT window and for one charge state. Returns index, scan number, RT,
precursor m/z, error in ppm, charge and intensity; open any hit with get_spectrum.

path.description: Run path relative to the data folder (from list_runs); may be omitted if there is one run

rt_end_min.description: Only use spectra at or before this RT (min)

rt_start_min.description: Only use spectra at or after this RT (min)

get_bpc.description:
Base peak chromatogram (intensity of the most intense peak per spectrum, with its m/z) vs
retention time, downsampled to `max_points`. Cleaner than the TIC for spotting eluting
compounds; the base-peak m/z tells you which ion dominates each part of the run.

max_points.description: Maximum points returned (downsampled, max per bin)

ms_level.description: MS level to use (1 = survey scans)

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing save_path file

path.description: Run path relative to the data folder (from list_runs); may be omitted if there is one run

rt_end_min.description: Only use spectra at or before this RT (min)

rt_start_min.description: Only use spectra at or after this RT (min)

Describe one run: instrument vendor/model/serial (when the file records them), acquisition
date, software, number of spectra per MS level, retention-time and m/z ranges, polarity,

(give exactly one). Returns MS level, RT, polarity, centroid/profile, precursor m/z and
charge for MS2, a summary (peak count, TIC, base peak, m/z range) and the `top_n` most
intense peaks; `save_path` writes the full peak list to CSV. For profile spectra the top
peaks are local maxima of the profile.

mz_max.description: Only consider peaks below this m/z

mz_min.description: Only consider peaks above this m/z

Parse an existing MassLynx, SCIEX OS, MassHunter or Xcalibur import file from the output

Insert blanks and QC injections and optionally randomise the run order (with a recorded seed).

re-applied whenever samples are added; data-file names follow the new run order.

List the supported import formats (Waters MassLynx, SCIEX OS, Agilent MassHunter, Thermo

characters Windows does not allow in file names, tray/vial position format and plate bounds,

Errors block export; warnings don't.

format.description: Validate for another vendor format (default: the draft's)

get_dispensed_volume.description: Return the accumulated infused and withdrawn volumes (pump command DIS).

get_status.description:
Report what the pump is doing (infusing/withdrawing/stopped/paused, alarms), the syringe
diameter, rate, target volume, direction and the accumulated dispensed volumes.

infuse.description:
Push `volume_ml` out of the syringe at `rate_ml_min`, then stop. Returns as soon as pumping
has started, with the estimated duration. Requires the correct syringe diameter (`set_syringe`)
and a stopped pump. Overwrites phases 1-2 of the pump's stored Pumping Program.

list_syringe_presets.description:
List the syringe inside diameters from the New Era manual's reference table (BD, Monoject,
Terumo, HSW Norm-Ject, Poulten & Graf glass, stainless steel, SGE, Hamilton), with the NE-1000
rate range each allows. Use a name with `set_syringe`.

contains.description: Only list presets whose name contains this text, e.g. 'BD'

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_syringe.description:
Set the syringe inside diameter, either from a preset or a measured value. The pump must be
stopped. Changing the diameter also resets the dispensed-volume accumulators and may switch the
pump's volume units (µL below 14.0 mm, mL above).

diameter_mm.description: Syringe inside diameter in mm (overrides preset)

preset.description: Syringe preset name from `list_syringe_presets`, e.g. 'BD 10 mL'

stop_pump.description: Stop the pump immediately (STP). A paused program is also cancelled so it cannot resume.

withdraw.description:
Pull `volume_ml` into the syringe at `rate_ml_min`, then stop. Returns as soon as pumping has
started. Make sure the syringe has room for the volume. Overwrites phases 1-2 of the pump's
stored Pumping Program.

get_connection_info.description:

whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_device_info.description:
Describe the connected device: analog input/output channels, digital lines, supported
voltage ranges, maximum sample rates, and the outputs this server has set. Call this before
choosing channels, ranges and rates.

list_devices.description:
List every NI-DAQmx device the driver can see (product type, serial number, channels,
whether it is an NI MAX simulated device) and which one this server is connected to.

read_analog.description:
Measure voltage on one or more analog inputs: a single on-demand reading, or a finite
hardware-timed acquisition of `samples` per channel at `rate_hz`. Returns per-channel
statistics and a downsampled waveform; optionally saves all data to CSV.

Bounded by the `max_samples`, `max_rate_hz` and `max_acquisition_s` limits; the device's own
maximum rate (shared by all channels on multiplexed devices) also applies. Blocks for
samples / rate_hz seconds.

max_points.description: Max points per channel in the returned waveform

max_v.description: Highest expected voltage (sets the input range)

min_v.description: Lowest expected voltage (sets the input range)

rate_hz.description: Sample clock rate per channel (required if samples > 1)

samples.description: Samples per channel; 1 = one on-demand reading

save_path.description: Write all samples to this new .csv file (never overwritten)

terminal_config.description: Input wiring: rse = single-ended to AI GND, diff = differential, nrse = to AI SENSE

read_digital_lines.description:
Read the logic level of digital lines.

Lines that this server is driving as outputs are reported from their last commanded level and
are NOT re-read: an NI-DAQmx digital-input task would switch them to inputs and release
whatever they drive. Reading a line another program drives may likewise make it an input.

read_thermocouple.description:
Measure temperature (°C) with thermocouples (types B, E, J, K, N, R, S, T) on a
thermocouple-capable device, e.g. an NI 9211/9212/9213/9214 module or USB-TC01.

Use cjc_source='built_in' on modules with a cold-junction sensor; 'constant' uses cjc_value_c
(accuracy then depends on how well you know the terminal temperature). Devices without
thermocouple support return an NI-DAQmx error.

channels.description: Thermocouple inputs, e.g. 'ai0' or 'ai0:3' (on a thermocouple-capable device/module)

cjc_source.description: 'built_in' = the module's cold-junction sensor (e.g. NI 9211/9213, USB-TC01); 'constant' = cjc_value_c

save_path.description: Write all samples to this new .csv file (never overwritten)

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_outputs_safe.description:
Put the device's outputs in a safe state: every analog output to 0 V (or the bottom of its
range if 0 V is not in it) and, by default, every digital line this server drove - plus the
`safe_do_lines` option lines - driven low. Use when finished or if anything looks wrong.

digital_low.description: Also drive low every DO line this server drove (and the safe_do_lines option)

write_analog.description:
Set an analog output to a DC voltage (static, software-timed). The output keeps this value
after the call on most NI devices, until changed or `set_outputs_safe` is called.

This energises whatever the output drives (valve or heater controllers, laser drivers,
actuators). Checked against `max_ao_voltage_v` (absolute value) and the device's AO range
(e.g. USB-6008/6009: 0-5 V) before anything is sent.

write_digital_lines.description:
Drive digital output lines high or low. The lines keep their level after the call until
changed or `set_outputs_safe` is called.

Digital outputs often switch relays, valves, pumps or trigger other instruments; confirm with
the user what each line controls. Voltage levels depend on the device (e.g. 5 V TTL or 3.3 V).

levels.description: One level for all lines, or one per line in order

max_acquisition_duration_s.description: Longest single acquisition (scans x integration time)

max_integration_time_ms.description: Longest integration time an agent may set

acquire_spectrum.description:
Acquire an intensity spectrum (raw counts) with optional averaging, boxcar smoothing and
corrections. Returns downsampled (wavelength, counts), summary statistics, the most
prominent peaks with FWHM, and a saturation check; `save_path` writes the full spectrum to a
new .csv file (an existing file is never overwritten).

boxcar_half_width.description: Boxcar smoothing: pixels averaged on EACH side (0 = off)

correct_dark_counts.description: Subtract the mean of the optically masked (electric dark) pixels

max_points.description: Maximum points returned (bin-averaged)

save_path.description: Optional new .csv file for the full-resolution data (existing files are not overwritten)

subtract_stored_dark.description: Subtract the stored dark spectrum (same settings required)

auto_integration_time.description:
Adjust the integration time until the brightest raw pixel (optionally within a wavelength
window) is within the target band of saturation (default 70-85 %). Stays within the device
limits and the `max_integration_time_ms` safety limit. Re-take dark/reference afterwards.

target_max_percent.description: Upper edge of the target band, % of saturation

target_min_percent.description: Lower edge of the target band, % of saturation

detector_cooling_off.description:
Switch the detector thermo-electric cooler off (the detector warms to ambient). Does
nothing on spectrometers without a TEC.

find_peaks.description:
Find peaks (or dips) with position, height, prominence and FWHM in the most recent
spectrum (intensity, absorbance or transmittance). Acquires a fresh intensity spectrum if
none has been taken yet.

min_prominence_fraction.description: Minimum prominence as a fraction of the data range

Model, serial, pixel count, wavelength range, integration-time limits, saturation level,
supported corrections, TEC presence, and which dark/reference spectra are stored.

list_spectrometers.description:
List the Ocean spectrometers seabreeze can see (model, serial number, whether open) and
which one this server is connected to. Use a serial number as `--address` to pick one.

measure_absorbance.description:
Measure the absorbance spectrum A = -log10((S - D) / (R - D)) of the sample now in the
beam, using the stored dark D and reference R (same settings). Ask the user to insert the
sample first. Also returns values at `wavelengths_nm` and the absorbance maxima.

max_points.description: Maximum points returned (bin-averaged)

save_path.description: Optional new .csv file for the full-resolution data (existing files are not overwritten)

wavelengths_nm.description: Wavelengths (nm) at which to report interpolated values

measure_transmittance.description:
Measure the transmittance spectrum %T = 100 (S - D) / (R - D) of the sample now in the
beam, using the stored dark and reference. Ask the user to insert the sample first. Also
returns values at `wavelengths_nm` and the deepest transmission dips.

max_points.description: Maximum points returned (bin-averaged)

save_path.description: Optional new .csv file for the full-resolution data (existing files are not overwritten)

wavelengths_nm.description: Wavelengths (nm) at which to report interpolated values

read_detector_temperature.description:
Read the detector temperature from the thermo-electric cooler (TE-cooled models such as
the QE Pro, when seabreeze exposes the thermo_electric feature for them).

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_detector_cooling.description:
Enable the detector thermo-electric cooler at `setpoint_c` (TE-cooled models only). The
detector takes minutes to settle; dark current (and noise) drops as it cools. The TEC can only
cool to roughly 15-40 °C below ambient (QE Pro manual). Checked against `min_tec_setpoint_c`.

set_integration_time.description:
Set the detector integration time (ms), within the device limits from `get_device_info`.
Stored dark/reference spectra become unusable until re-taken at the new time.

store_dark_reference.description:
Record and store a DARK spectrum (kept in memory) for absorbance/transmittance.
BEFORE calling, ask the user to BLOCK THE LIGHT PATH (close the shutter, switch the lamp off
or cap the fiber) and wait for confirmation. Uses the present integration time.

boxcar_half_width.description: Boxcar smoothing: pixels averaged on EACH side (0 = off)

store_reference.description:
Record and store the REFERENCE (100 % transmission) spectrum in memory. BEFORE calling,
ask the user to put the BLANK (solvent-filled or empty cuvette) in the beam with the light on,
and wait for confirmation. Use the same settings as the dark.

boxcar_half_width.description: Boxcar smoothing: pixels averaged on EACH side (0 = off)

max_shake_speed_rpm.description: Fastest Heater-Shaker speed a protocol may request

deactivate_modules.description:
Switch attached modules off: stop heating/cooling (Temperature Module, Thermocycler block and
lid, Heater-Shaker heater), stop shaking, and lower Magnetic Module magnets. Only possible when
no run is in progress: stop the run first.

module_ids.description: Module IDs from list_modules; omit to switch off all modules

E-stop state, and the current run. Call this first to check the robot is ready.

Report a run's status, the step it is on, progress, recent steps and any errors, plus advice on
what to do next (e.g. when the run is waiting for error recovery).

recent_commands.description: How many recent steps to include

run_id.description: Run ID; omit for the current run

home_robot.description:
Home all axes of the robot (the gantry and pipettes move to their home positions). Refused
while a run is active. Make sure nothing is in the robot's path and the door is closed.

list_instruments.description:
List attached pipettes (and the Flex gripper): mount, name, channels, volume range, and whether
a tip is detected and calibration data exists.

list_modules.description:
List attached modules (Temperature Module, Heater-Shaker, Thermocycler, Magnetic Module,
Absorbance Plate Reader, ...) with live temperatures, targets, shake speed and status.

list_protocols.description: List protocols stored on the robot (newest last) with their analysis status and result.

list_runs.description: List recent protocol runs, newest first, with their status.

pause_run.description:
Pause a running protocol. The robot finishes its current step and then holds; resume_run
continues it.

run_id.description: Run ID; omit for the current run

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

resume_run.description:
Resume a paused run (the robot starts moving again), or leave error recovery. Refused while the
door is open. For a run awaiting recovery, `error_recovery` must be given.

error_recovery.description: Only for runs awaiting error recovery, after the user physically checked the robot: 'continue' resumes from the robot's current state (the failed step is skipped); 'assume_false_positive' treats the failure as a false alarm (e.g. the tip really was picked up)

run_id.description: Run ID; omit for the current run

set_lights.description: Turn the robot's deck (rail) lights on or off.

on.description: True to turn the deck lights on

start_run.description:
Create a run of an analyzed protocol and start it: the robot begins moving and pipetting.
Refused unless the protocol's analysis completed without errors, its module setpoints are within
the safety limits, no other run is active, the door is closed and the E-stop is released.

protocol_id.description: Protocol ID from upload_protocol or list_protocols

Stop (cancel) a run immediately. A stopped run cannot be resumed; the robot homes and drops
any attached tips into the trash. Use this whenever something looks wrong.

Upload a protocol file (plus optional custom labware) to the robot. The robot analyzes it
(simulates it) and this tool returns the analysis: errors, deck layout and whether it is ready

the cell is switched off. Safe to call when nothing is running.

Returns the data (time from the instrument timer) plus first/last/mean current and the charge.

Run a cyclic voltammogram: begin -> vertex 1 -> vertex 2 -> begin, `n_scans` times, and return
potential/current/time data with the anodic and cathodic peaks of every scan. Applies potential
to the cell for the whole scan; the cell is switched off at the end.

potential and return the data with the peak current and peak potential. The scan rate must be
below step / pulse_time / 2. Applies potential to the cell.

Advanced: run a raw MethodSCRIPT and return its raw output and decoded data packages. Literal
potentials of set_e / set_range_minmax da and the CV, LSV, DPV, SWV, NPV, ACV, CA, PAD, EIS and
fast CV/CA techniques are checked against `max_potential_v`, and literal `set_range ba` /
`set_autoranging ba` currents against `max_current_range_a`; values computed at run time are
not. Aborted after `timeout_s`; add `on_finished:` + `cell_off` to your script so the cell is
switched off after an abort. After a runtime error, a timeout or `abort_measurement` the server
switches the cell off itself.

script.description: MethodSCRIPT, one command per line (a leading 'e' line is ignored)

timeout_s.description: Abort the script after this

max_switch_on_pressure_mbar.description: Highest measured pressure at which an ionisation gauge may be switched on

instrument (newest last). Useful for debugging and for recording what was done.

whether the server is read-only, and the active safety limits. Call this first.

get_errors.description:
Read (and clear) the controller's ERROR word: controller error, no hardware, inadmissible
parameter or syntax error. An empty list means no error.

get_gauge_types.description:
List the gauge connected to each channel (TID), what kind it is, and whether it is an
ionisation gauge that is currently switched on or off (SEN).

log_pressure_series.description:
Log pressures at a fixed interval (e.g. a pump-down curve, leak-up/rate-of-rise test or
bake-out). Returns per-channel statistics in log-space plus a downsampled series; the full
series can be written to a new CSV file (an existing file is never overwritten). Bounded by
`max_log_duration_s` and 2 h per call.

duration_s.description: How long to log (at most 2 h per call)

max_points.description: Points returned per channel

save_path.description: Optional CSV file for every reading

read_all_pressures.description: Read every channel of the controller at once (PRX), with status per channel.

read_pressure.description: Read one gauge channel: status, pressure in the display unit and in mbar.

reconnect.description:
Close and re-open the connection to the instrument (e.g. after it was power
cycled or a cable was re-plugged).

set_gauge_power.description:
Switch an ionisation gauge (IKR, PKR, PBR, IMR) on or off (SEN). Switching a hot or cold
cathode gauge on at high pressure can burn out the filament or contaminate the gauge, so
switching ON is refused unless a valid reading from this gauge or `reference_channel` is at or
below `max_switch_on_pressure_mbar`. Switching off may trip setpoint relays used as interlocks.

on.description: True = switch the gauge on, False = off

reference_channel.description: Another gauge on the same vacuum (e.g. a Pirani) used to check the pressure

set_unit.description:
Change the pressure unit used on the display and interface (UNI). Readings in mbar are
always included regardless of this setting.

unit.description: Display/interface unit (TPG 26x: mbar, Pa or Torr only)

switch_gauge_off.description:
Switch an ionisation gauge off (e.g. before venting, or if the pressure is rising). Always
allowed. Note that setpoint relays assigned to this channel may change state.

channel.description: Channel of the ionisation gauge to switch off

max_memory_points.description: Most points read from acquisition memory in one capture

autoscale.description:
Run the scope's automatic setup (AUTO key): it picks vertical scales, timebase and trigger
for the connected signals. This overwrites the user's current setup - only use it when asked.
Needs signals of roughly >20 mVpp and >40 Hz.

capture_waveform.description:
Capture a channel's waveform, scaled to volts and seconds with the scope's waveform preamble,
and return statistics plus a downsampled trace; optionally save all points to CSV.

'memory' mode reads the whole record (bounded by the `max_memory_points` limit) in batches and
requires the scope to be stopped; 'screen' works while running.

max_points.description: Max points returned (the data is downsampled)

mode.description: 'screen' = the displayed points (1000-1200); 'memory' = full acquisition memory (scope must be stopped)

save_path.description: Write every point (time_s, volts) to this new .csv file (never overwritten)

force_trigger.description: Force one trigger (FORCE key). Only has an effect in NORMal or SINGle sweep while waiting.
